description: Conditional birthday branch: if Mom already revealed C02, Mark acknowledges it; otherwise he reveals the 40th birthday and the intoxicated voicemail together.

openingMessages.speaker: Mark
openingMessages.text: Hey, by the way. Did you ever figure out what happened that weekend?

choices.text: I know it was my birthday. I still don't remember much of it.
You mentioned I was celebrating. What was I celebrating?
Can we talk about something else?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yeah, your big four-oh! Forty years old, man. Welcome to the club.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I was going to give you a hard time about it, but after that voicemail, I figured I'd let you recover first.

choices.text: You said I sounded pretty drunk.
I still don't remember much of it.
What else did I say in that voicemail?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: That's putting it mildly. You kept apologizing about something. You didn't really sound happy.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I wish I'd been able to pick up when you called.

lines.speaker: Detective
lines.text: Saturday night, intoxication, repeated apologies. Keep following the thread.

choices.text: Did I say what I was apologizing for?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yeah, I figured. Forty is a big milestone, but I didn't think you'd want to erase the whole celebration.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I'm not making fun of you, by the way. You didn't sound like yourself.

choices.text: What else did I say in that voicemail?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Seriously? Bjarne, you turned forty this weekend. Saturday. Your fortieth birthday, and you don't remember it?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Wow. No way you drank so much you forgot the reason you were drinking.

lines.speaker: Pragmatist
lines.text: Forty. Apparently we've reached the age where our own save files are corrupted.

choices.text: I really don't remember any of it.
I appreciate you telling me. What happened after I called?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I could barely make out what you were saying. You kept apologizing and saying you'd messed things up.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Look, I'm not trying to make fun of you. I just wish I'd picked up when you called.

choices.text: I appreciate you worrying about me.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Not really. You kept repeating something about having messed things up.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I think you said, 'I don't know how to fix it.' Then you started rambling about something else.

choices.text: I wish I knew what I meant.
Thanks for telling me. I appreciate it.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Maybe not. Still wish I could've been there.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Dude, no. You sounded like someone who was having a rough night. There's a difference.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Don't make it weird, man. You're my best friend. It's part of the job.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Sure. We don't have to talk about it right now.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just promise me you'll listen to that voicemail when you're ready.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Anytime, man.
